1. BitLocker and BitLocker To Go: BitLocker is a Windows tool that encrypts a drive.
Encryption protects data if a computer is lost or stolen.
The user may need a password, PIN, USB key or TPM to unlock the drive.
BitLocker To Go is used for USB flash drives and other removable drives.
A BitLocker Recovery Key can unlock the drive when normal login does not work.
The Recovery Key can be stored in a Microsoft account, company account or by the IT department.
Do not turn off BitLocker or remove encryption without permission in a company.
2. Windows Updates: Windows Update keeps Windows secure and stable.
Quality Updates fix security and reliability problems.
Feature Updates add new Windows features and larger changes.
Driver and Firmware Updates can improve hardware support.
Optional Updates are not always installed automatically.
The computer may need a restart after an update.
You can check updates in Settings > Windows Update.
3. Device Driver and Firmware Updates: A driver helps Windows communicate with hardware.
Drivers are used for devices such as graphics cards, network adapters, printers and sound devices.
A driver update can fix bugs, security problems and compatibility problems.
You can check drivers in Device Manager.
If a new driver causes a problem, Windows may allow you to use Roll Back Driver.
Firmware is software stored inside a hardware device.
Firmware updates can improve stability, security or hardware support.
Firmware updates must be installed carefully because a failed update can cause serious problems.
4. Application Updates: Updates can fix bugs and security problems.
Updates can also improve compatibility with Windows.
Some applications have a Check for updates option.
Browsers and security software are usually updated often.
Keep business applications updated according to company rules.
5. Browser Cache: A browser cache stores parts of websites on the computer.
The cache helps websites load faster.
Old or damaged cache files can cause website problems.
A page may look wrong or show old information.
Clearing the browser cache can fix some loading and display problems.
After clearing the cache, reload the website and test it again.
6. Task Manager: Task Manager helps you check running applications and system performance.
Open Task Manager with Ctrl + Shift + Esc.
The Processes tab shows running applications and background processes.
The Performance tab shows CPU, memory, disk and network usage.
The Startup apps tab shows programs that start with Windows.
The Users tab shows users who are logged in.
The Details tab shows more information about processes.
The Services tab shows Windows services.
You can use Task Manager to close an application that is not responding.
Do not stop unknown system processes if you do not know what they do.
7. Data Loss and Cloud Backup: Data loss means important files are lost or damaged.
Data can be lost because of hardware failure, accidental deletion or a cyberattack.
A backup is a second copy of important data.
Cloud storage can keep files on remote servers.
Cloud files can often be opened from different devices.
Common cloud storage services include OneDrive, Google Drive and Dropbox.
A backup is useful when a computer is lost, damaged or reset.
8. OneDrive: OneDrive is Microsoft's cloud storage service.
Users can sync folders between the computer and the cloud.
Files can be opened from another device after signing in.
Deleted files may be restored from the OneDrive Recycle Bin.
If OneDrive does not sync, check the Internet connection first.
Check the OneDrive icon in the system tray for an error message.
Restart OneDrive if synchronization is not working.
Check that there is enough cloud storage space.
9. Google Drive for Desktop: Google Drive for Desktop connects Windows with Google Drive.
Users can store files in the cloud and sync folders.
Stream files keeps most files in the cloud and uses less local disk space.
Mirror files keeps files both on the computer and in the cloud.
Files can be managed from the Google Drive folder in Windows.
Check the Google Drive icon in the system tray if synchronization has a problem.
Check the Internet connection and available storage space.
10. Dropbox for Desktop: Dropbox is a cloud storage and synchronization service.
The Dropbox application creates a Dropbox folder in Windows.
Files in this folder can sync with the cloud.
Changes can also sync to other connected devices.
Selective Sync lets the user choose which folders are stored on the computer.
This can help save local disk space.
If Dropbox does not sync, check the Internet connection, application status and available storage.
11. BIOS, UEFI and Windows Boot: BIOS and UEFI are firmware that start before Windows.
BIOS or UEFI checks hardware and starts the boot process.
The boot order tells the computer which device to start from first.
The main system drive is normally the first boot device.
A technician may change the boot order to start from a USB drive.
This can be useful for Windows installation or recovery tools.
Common keys to open BIOS or UEFI include F2, F10, Esc and Delete.
The correct key depends on the computer manufacturer.
Be careful when changing BIOS or UEFI settings.
12. Safe Mode and Windows Recovery Envir: Safe Mode starts Windows with only basic drivers and services.
It is useful for troubleshooting startup problems, driver problems and software conflicts.
If the problem does not happen in Safe Mode, a third-party driver or application may be the cause.
You can open recovery options from Settings > System > Recovery > Advanced startup.
You can also hold Shift and select Restart.
Windows may open the Windows Recovery Environment automatically after repeated startup failures.
In WinRE, open Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings.
Basic Safe Mode uses only essential drivers.
Safe Mode with Networking also loads network support.
Safe Mode with Command Prompt opens a command-line troubleshooting environment.
